entities.label: Person
entities.summary: Adurbad-i Mahraspand was an influential Zoroastrian high priest during the reign of the Sasanian king (shah) Shapur II. Born into a prominent family, he rose to prominence through his exceptional wisdom, piety, and administrative skills. As Shapur II's chief priest, Adurbad-i Mahraspand played a crucial role in shaping the king's policies, particularly regarding the persecution of Christians and Jews. He also oversaw the construction of numerous temples, monuments, and infrastructure projects throughout the Sasanian Empire. Adurbad-i Mahraspand's legacy extended beyond his lifetime, as his successors continued to shape the religious and cultural landscape of the empire. His contributions to the development of Zoroastrianism and the Sasanian Empire's administrative systems have left a lasting impact on the region's history. The ruins of his temple in Firuzabad, Iran, remain a testament to his enduring legacy.
